newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to study German court verdict on Iran.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to study German court verdict on Iran.

text.p: Turkey said on Monday it would study a German court verdict last week linking neighbour Iran to the killing of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin before deciding on a response to the ruling.

The Turkish foreign ministry said its ties with Iran were closer than those of European countries, despite a dispute between Ankara and Tehran this year which led to the mutual expulsion of diplomats.

"Given the fact that Turkey is a country of the region and a neighbouring country with Iran we have much closer and directly interested parametres in our relationship with Iran," ministry spokesman Omer Akbel told a news conference in English.
Most European Union countries have responed to a German court ruling that Iran ordered the 1992 murders of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin by summoning their ambassadors for consultations.

Relations between Ankara and Tehran were strained in March by Iran's alleged support for Islamist militancy in Turkey, but agreement was later reached to fill empty ambassador seats in the two capitals.
The Turkish army is also uneasy about what it says is Iran's efforts to stockpile weapons of mass destruction and its alleged support for Kurdish rebels in southeast Turkey.
"We in Turkey have suffered a lot from terrorism and we have always acted very decidedly against acts of terrorism and violence," Akbel said when asked about the Berlin court verdict.
"We also wish to obtain, when released, the detailed verdict of the court and study it," he said.
Turkey and Iran last year signed a $23 billion, 23-year natural gas supply deal, drawing strong criticism from the United States.
Akbel said the latest international row had not so far affected the prospects for the pipeline, on which construction has already begun.
"As it stands now the project is still valid and underway."
